Rashi on Pesachim 45a:12:1.english: And similarly, with regard to ritual impurity - [It is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:13:1.hebrew: ה"ג: ל"ש אלא במקום שאין עשוי לחזק, אבל במקום העשוי לחזק אינו חייב לבער; מכלל דפחות מכזית, אפילו במקום שאין עשוי לחזק אינו חייב לבער - ופירש: לא שנו דכזית במקום אחד חייב לבער אלא שאין הסדקין בשולי עריבה, מקום הצקת מים, שיהא בצק זה מועיל לעריבה לחזק המים, אלא בדפנותיהן — מקום שאין עשוי לחזק. אבל אם במקום העשוי לחזק הן, בטלו לגבה והוו כעץ, דמסתמא בטלינהו האי גברא להתם, ואפילו כזית אינו חייב לבער:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:13:1.english: This is the reading: They taught [this] only in a place that does not serve to reinforce, but in a place that serves to reinforce, one is not obligated to remove [it]; by implication, less than an olive-bulk, even in a place that does not serve to reinforce, one is not obligated to remove [it] - And [the] explanation [is]: They taught that [for] an olive-bulk in one place one is obligated to remove [it] only when the cracks are not at the bottom of the kneading trough — the place where water is poured, where this dough would be useful to the kneading trough to hold the water — but rather in its walls, a place that does not serve to reinforce. However, if they are in a place that serves to reinforce, they become nullified to it and are like wood, since this person presumably nullified them there, and even [if there is] an olive-bulk, he is not obligated to remove [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:14:1.hebrew: מכלל דפחות מכזית כו' - ותלמודא דייק ממילתא דשמואל, דאוקמה למתני' במקום שאין עשוי לחזק, וקתני מתני' בפחות מיכן בטל במיעוטו. שמע מינה דפחות מכזית לא חשיב, ואע"ג דאיכא בה פלגי זיתא טובא, הואיל ולאו במקום אחד נינהו — לא חשיבי:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:14:1.english: This proves by inference that [with regard to] less than an olive-bulk, etc. - And the Gemara infers [this] from Shmuel's statement, who established the Mishnah [as referring to] a place where it does not serve to reinforce, and the Mishnah teaches [that] with less than this [amount], it is nullified due to its insignificance. Learn from this that less than an olive-bulk is not significant, and even though there are many half-olives in it, since they are not in one place, they are not significant.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:15:1.hebrew: ה"ג: איכא דמתני לה אסיפא, פחות מיכן בטל במיעוטו, אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: לא שנו אלא במקום העשוי לחזק, אבל במקום שאין עשוי לחזק חייב לבער, מכלל דכזית אפילו במקום העשוי לחזק חייב לבער - ואע"ג דודאי מבטיל ליה, אפילו הכי כיון דחשיב לא בטיל. ולישנא בתרא חמיר מקמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:15:1.english: We read the text thus: Some teach [it] with regard to the latter clause: [If it is] less than this, it is nullified due to its insignificance. Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel: They taught [this] only in a place where it serves to reinforce [the bowl], but in a place where it does not serve to reinforce, one is obligated to remove [it]; by inference, [if there is] an olive-bulk, even in a place where it serves to reinforce, one is obligated to remove [it] - And even though he certainly nullifies it, nevertheless, since it is significant, it is not nullified. And the latter version is stricter than the first.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:1:1.hebrew: משום - דבדוכתא אחריתי נמי כתבה רחמנא, ושני כתובין הבאין כו'. אבל לרבנן, דמוקי לה לטעם כעיקר, לא הוו שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, כדמפרש לקמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:1:1.english: Because - in another place as well the Merciful One wrote [it], and two verses that come [as one do not teach], etc. However, according to the Rabbis, who establish it [to teach that] flavor is like the substance, they are not two verses that come as one, as [the Gemara] explains further on.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:2:1.hebrew: כל אשר יגע בבשרה - בשר חולין או שלמים שזמן אכילתו מרובה מחטאת, ונגע בחטאת, יקדש, כדמפרש להיות כמוה. שאם פסולה היתה החטאת, כגון פיגול או פסול אחר, תיפסל אף זו שבלעה ממנה. ואם כשירה היא החטאת, מהניא לבולעת הימנה לאסור באכילה אלא כחמור שבה — כחומר החטאת שנבלע בה — לפנים מן הקלעים, ולזכרי כהונה, וליום ולילה אחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:2:1.english: Anything that touches in its flesh - [This refers to] non-sacred meat or [meat of] a peace-offering, whose allotted time for eating is greater than [that of] a sin-offering, and it touched a sin-offering; it shall become consecrated, as it explains, to be like it. For if the sin-offering was disqualified, such as [by] piggul or another disqualification, this [meat] that absorbed from it also becomes disqualified. And if the sin-offering is valid, it affects [the meat] that absorbs from it to forbid [it] from being eaten except according to its stringency — [that is,] like the stringency of the sin-offering that was absorbed within it — within the curtains [of the Courtyard], and to male priests, and for one day and one night.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:2:2.hebrew: יכול אפילו לא בלעה - הנוגעת בה ממנה, קאמר רחמנא יקדש, ת"ל כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:2:2.english: [I] might [have thought] even if it did not absorb - [i.e., the piece] touching it [did not absorb] from it, [nevertheless] the Merciful One says "shall become consecrated"; [therefore] the verse states, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:3:1.hebrew: תאכל - הבולעת כחמור שבה, שהרי יש בה ב' מינין — אחד חמור ואחד קל — וכלה הולכת אחר החמור. אלמא היתר מצטרף לאיסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:3:1.english: May be eaten - [That is, the piece] that absorbed [from the sin-offering is eaten] in accordance with the more stringent [standards] of it, for behold, there are two types [of substance] in it — one stringent and one lenient — and all of it follows the stringent [one]. Thus, a permitted [substance] combines with a prohibited [substance].

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג ורבנן אמרי לך מיצרך צריכי - חטאת אשמועינן משום דהיתר מצטרף לאיסור, ואי נמי לא איבלע בכולה, אי אכל חצי זית פיגול וחצי זית היתר בבת אחת, ניגמור מינה דבקדשים ניחייב. ומיהו בשאר איסורין לא אמרינן הכי, ואפילו בנזיר, דחולין מקדשים לא גמרינן. ומשרת לאו לאגמורי היתר מצטרף לאיסור אתא בנזיר, אלא ליתן טעם כעיקר, דמגיעולי נכרים לא יליף דחידוש הוא, ואיצטריך למכתביה בנזיר, ומכאן אתה דן לכל התורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:1.english: This is the reading: And the Rabbis say to you, they are necessary - [The verse of] the sin-offering teaches us [its law] regarding a permitted [substance] joining together with a prohibited [substance] — that even if [the prohibited substance] was not absorbed throughout all of it, if one ate a half-olive-bulk of piggul and a half-olive-bulk of permitted [food] at the same time, we derive from it that with consecrated [foods] he is liable. However, regarding other prohibitions we do not say this — and even regarding a nazirite — because we do not derive [laws of] non-sacred [food] from consecrated [offerings]. And [the term] "soaked" [mishrat] does not come to teach [that] a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance] regarding a nazirite; rather, [it comes] to teach [that] taste is like the substance itself — for [this] cannot be derived from [vessels] purged from gentiles, since that is a novel law — so it was necessary to write it regarding a nazirite, and from here you derive [the principle] for the entire Torah.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:2.hebrew: מיצרך צריכי - תרוויהו, כדמפרש לקמיה. ולא הוו שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, דחד מחבריה לא מצי יליף דנימא: מדהדר כתביה לאידך ולא ילפא מחבריה, ש"מ דווקא — הכי קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:2.english: They are necessary - Both of them [are necessary], as [the Gemara] explains further on. And they are not two verses that come as one, for one cannot be derived from the other such that we would say: "Since [Scripture] wrote the other one as well and did not derive [it] from its counterpart, learn from this [that the law applies] specifically [to these cases]" — this is what [the Gemara] means.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:3.hebrew: חולין - להחמיר לא גמרי מדין קדשים, דדין קדשים להיות חמורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:7:3.english: Non-sacred [food] - [It] does not derive from the law of consecrated [items] to be stringent, for the law of consecrated [items] is to be stringent.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:8:1.hebrew: ור' עקיבא - אית ליה גיעולי נכרים לאו חידוש הוא, דלא מצריך קרא לטעם כעיקר. הלכך, לר"ע, כיון דשמעת ליה דמפיק "משרת" להיתר מצטרף לאיסור, על כרחיך תרווייהו הני להיתר מצטרף לאיסור אתו, והוה ליה חטאת קרא יתירא דמצי למיגמר מנזיר, והוו להו שני כתובין הבאין כאחד. ומש"ה פשיטא ליה לר' יוחנן דר"ע לא גמר שאר איסורין מנזיר, דהא לא מצי, דשני כתובין נינהו. והא ליכא למימר "משרת" להיתר מצטרף לאיסור וחטאת לטעם כעיקר, דגיעולי נכרים חידוש הוא ולא מצי גמר חטאת מינייהו ואין כאן שני כתובין — דא"כ טעם כעיקר בשאר איסורין מנא ליה? מגיעולי נכרים לא גמרינן, מקדשים נמי לא גמרינן. ורבנן דפליגי עליה דר"א בכותח הבבלי — אלמא לית להו טעם כעיקר דאורייתא — מפקי להאי "משרת" להיתר מצטרף לאיסור כר"ע, ובגיעולי נכרים סבירא להו דחידוש הוא כרבנן. והכי אמרינן נמי ב"כל הבשר" דאיכא למאן דאמר טעמו ולא ממשו דרבנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:8:1.english: And Rabbi Akiva - He holds that [the prohibition of] vessels used by gentiles is not an anomaly, as he does not require a verse for [the principle that] taste is like the substance. Therefore, according to Rabbi Akiva, since you have heard that he derives from "soaked" [that] a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance], perforce both of these [verses] come [to teach that] a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance], and [the verse of] the sin-offering is a superfluous verse, since it could be derived from a nazirite; thus they are two verses that come as one. And for this reason it is obvious to Rabbi Yochanan that Rabbi Akiva does not derive other prohibitions from a nazirite, because he cannot, as they are two verses [that come as one]. And one cannot say [that] "soaked" [teaches] that a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance], and the sin-offering [teaches] that taste is like the substance, [and] that vessels used by gentiles is an anomaly so one cannot derive the sin-offering from them and [thus] there are not two verses [that come as one] here — because if so, from where would he [derive that] taste is like the substance for other prohibitions? From vessels used by gentiles we do not derive [it], [and] from consecrated [offerings] we also do not derive [it]. And the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer regarding Babylonian kutach — which shows that they do not hold [that] taste is like the substance by Torah law — derive this [word] "soaked" [to teach that] a permitted [substance] joins together with a prohibited [substance], like Rabbi Akiva, and regarding vessels used by gentiles they hold that it is an anomaly, like the Rabbis. And so too we say in [the chapter] Kol HaBasar that there is one who says [that] its taste without its substance is [prohibited only] by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:9:1.hebrew: לימד על איסורי נזיר כו' - מדכיילינהו לחרצנים וזגין בחדא אכילה, לימד שמצטרפין:
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:9:1.english: Taught with regard to prohibitions of a nazirite, etc. - Since [Scripture] included grape seeds and grape skins in a single [prohibition of] eating, it taught that they combine.

Rashi on Pesachim 45a:9:2.hebrew: השתא לרבי עקיבא - ל"ל דכתב רחמנא קרא להכי? השתא איסור והיתר מצטרפין כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 45a:9:2.english: Now, according to Rabbi Akiva - Why do I need the Merciful One to write a verse for this? Now, [if] prohibited and permitted [substances] join together, etc.

Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:13:1.hebrew: כאן שלא במקום לישה - פ"ה דשלא במקום לישה עובר בפחות מכזית. וקשה, דאמר לקמן: "לא אמרן אלא בעריבה, אבל בבית חייב לבער, משום דזימנין דמיכנף ונפלי אהדדי", ולפ"ה תיפוק ליה דפחות מכזית חייב לבער שלא במקום לישה? ונראה לר"י דמקום העשוי לחזק היינו את הכלי — בין במקום לישה ובין שלא במקום לישה עושין לחזק; אך במקום לישה יש להחמיר יותר, שיש לחוש שידבק מאותה עיסה לעיסה אחרת על ידי לישה, או תבלע מן הטעם. ולכך כזית במקום לישה, אפילו עשוי לחזק, עובר — אף על גב דודאי מבטלו — כיון דאיכא תרתי לריעותא: כזית ובמקום לישה. ופחות מכזית, אפילו במקום לישה, אי עשוי לחזק — לא גזרו ביה רבנן, דכיון שהוא דבר מועט, יכול לשמור שלא ילוש עליו. וכן כזית שלא במקום לישה, אי עשוי לחזק — אין עובר. אבל פחות מכזית ושלא במקום לישה, אפילו אין עשויה לחזק, מותר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:13:1.english: "Here, not in the place of kneading" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that [when the dough is] not in the place of kneading, one transgresses [even] with less than an olive-bulk. And [this is] difficult, for [the Gemara] states later: "We only said [that less than an olive-bulk is nullified] in a kneading bowl, but in a house one is obligated to remove [it], because sometimes they gather and fall together" — yet according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], let it emerge [directly] that one is obligated to remove less than an olive-bulk when not in the place of kneading [even in a kneading bowl]! And it appears to Ri [Rabbenu Yitzchak] that "a place that serves to reinforce" means [reinforcing] the vessel — both in the place of kneading and not in the place of kneading, people use [dough] to reinforce [it]; however, in the place of kneading one must be more stringent, for there is concern that [some] of that dough will stick to another dough through kneading, or that [the other dough] will absorb some of its taste. Therefore, an olive-bulk in the place of kneading, even if it serves to reinforce, one transgresses [for it] — even though he certainly nullifies it — since there are two detrimental factors: [it is] an olive-bulk and [it is] in the place of kneading. And [as for] less than an olive-bulk, even in the place of kneading, if it serves to reinforce, the Rabbis did not decree regarding it, because since it is a small amount, he can be careful not to knead upon it. And similarly, an olive-bulk not in the place of kneading, if it serves to reinforce, one does not transgress. However, less than an olive-bulk that is not in the place of kneading, even if it does not serve to reinforce, is permitted.

Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:1:1.hebrew: משום דהוי נזיר וחטאת שני כתובין הבאין כאחד - תימה לרשב"א: אמאי לא קאמר נזיר וחמץ, דר"ע דריש "כל" בפ' התערובת (זבחים דף פב.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:1:1.english: Because a nazirite and a sin-offering are two verses that come as one - The Rashba wonders why [the Gemara] does not say "a nazirite and leavened bread [chametz]," for Rabbi Akiva expounds [the word] "kol" [any] in the chapter [entitled] HaTa'arovet (Zevachim 82a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:4:1.hebrew: <abbr title="רבינו חננאל">ר"ח</abbr> גרס "כחומר שבהן", ומיירי בחטאת ושלמים: ואם נבלע החטאת בשלמים שנשחט אתמול — נאכל כחומר השלמים, ואינו נאכל בלילה; ואם נבלע החטאת בשלמים שנשחט היום — נאכל כחומר החטאת, ואינו נאכל למחר. ולשון הברייתא קשה, דאמר "עד שיבלע בבשרה" — משמע דאיירי בהיתר שנבלע באיסור, והדר קאמר "יקדש להיות כמוה" — משמע שהאיסור נבלע בהיתר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:4:1.english: Rabbeinu Chananel reads "according to the more stringent of them," and [the baraita] is speaking of a sin-offering and a peace-offering: if [the taste of] the sin-offering was absorbed into a peace-offering that was slaughtered yesterday, it is eaten according to the stringency of the peace-offering, and may not be eaten at night; and if [the taste of] the sin-offering was absorbed into a peace-offering that was slaughtered today, it is eaten according to the stringency of the sin-offering, and may not be eaten the next day. However, the wording of the baraita is difficult, for it states "until it is absorbed into its flesh," which implies that it is speaking of a permitted [substance] that was absorbed into a forbidden [substance], and then it states "it shall become consecrated to be like it," which implies that the forbidden [substance] was absorbed into the permitted [substance].

Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:5:1.hebrew: ורבנן אמרי לך חטאת להיתר מצטרף לאיסור - אור"י דבנזיר בפ' ג' מינין (דף ל':) משמע נזיר וחטאת לרבנן תרווייהו לטעם כעיקר, דקאמר התם צריכ': דאי כתב רחמנא חטאת — חולין מקדשים לא גמרינן; ואי כתב רחמנא נזיר — חטאת מנזיר לא ילפינן, דחמיר איסוריה, דאפילו חרצן אסיר ליה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:5:1.english: "And the Rabbis say to you [that] a sin-offering [teaches that] permitted [food] combines with forbidden [food]" - R"I says that in Nazir, in the chapter [entitled] Sheloshah Minim (30b), it is implied [that] both nazirite and sin-offering according to the Rabbis [are] for [the principle that] taste is like the substance, for [the Gemara] says there [that both are] necessary: for if the Merciful One had written [it only for] a sin-offering, we would not derive non-sacred [prohibitions] from consecrated [things]; and if the Merciful One had written [it only for] a nazirite, we would not derive a sin-offering from a nazirite, because its prohibition is more stringent, as even a grape seed is forbidden to him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:5:2.hebrew: בשמעתין משמע דטעם כעיקר דאורייתא, דילפינן מנזיר דלאו אסמכתא היא, דמדר"ע דאמר לקי אהיתר מצטרף לאיסור בנזיר — נשמע לרבנן. וקשה מפ' כל הבשר (חולין דף קח.) וממסכת ע"ג (דף סז:), ושם מפורש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 45a:5:2.english: In our sugya it is implied that [the principle that] "flavor is like the substance itself" (ta'am ke'ikar) is of biblical authority, for we derive [it] from [the laws of] a nazirite — [meaning] that it is not a mere asmakhta [rabbinic support] — since from Rabbi Akiva, who says one is flogged for permitted [food] combining with forbidden [food] regarding a nazirite, we learn [the same] for the Rabbis. However, [this] is difficult from the chapter Kol HaBasar (Chullin 108a) and from Tractate Avodah Zarah (67b), and it is explained there.
